protocol.step1_frozen_hypothesis: Transport debris left by prior packaging runs is mechanically detectable and distinguishable from live surfaces.
protocol.step3_independent_execution: executed transport_debris_detector.py and test_transport_debris_detector.py myself under python3 -I, before reading manifest.json/result.json conclusions

independent_execution.corroboration: git ls-tree -r --name-only 1e6f53c323f8326d12af213557082a3665991f19 -- packs, run independently in the review-b worktree, returns 93 real files under packs/. This directly confirms packs/** exists with real content at the pinned commit, exactly as the task brief flagged.

critical_finding_stale_and_false_record.description: The unit's git history (git log --oneline -- workstreams/po03/attempts/po03-wa-b2e7-034-transport-debris-detector/) shows 5 commits: dfe20d0 (initial, verdict PASS) -> af40421 (result) -> 0b935b9 (verdict flipped to NOT_SUPPORTED, added observed_surface_boundary.txt claiming 'packs ABSENT') -> c010ffe (boundary result) -> d35c889 (tip: added scan_git_tree(), a third test proving packs IS present with 93 real entries, per_surface_verdicts.json, and real_pack_output.json showing packs 'PRESENT_BUT_UNRESOLVED' with entry_count 93). The manifest.json and result.json AT THE BRANCH TIP still point to the OLD commit 0b935b9c76b372e592602f16f050a34f77a86d4d, still claim only 2 tests ran, still assert verdict NOT_SUPPORTED with evidence text 'packs ABSENT', and do NOT list per_surface_verdicts.json or real_pack_output.json as artifacts -- even though both files are committed in the same owned subtree at the branch tip.
critical_finding_stale_and_false_record.conclusion: The blanket NOT_SUPPORTED verdict citing 'packs ABSENT' is over-generalized and factually false, refuted by the producer's own later, committed work in the identical subtree. This is a manifest-completeness violation (2 real committed artifacts are absent from the manifest's artifact list) and a case of a false claim left standing as the final recorded evidence.

hidden_case.description: Tested whether a file explicitly named 'live' by the pointer graph (live_paths) but bearing a debris-like suffix (e.g. a legitimately current 'release.stage' file) is correctly classified as live, since the falsifiable hypothesis is specifically about distinguishing debris from live surfaces using evidence including pointer paths.
hidden_case.command: scan([root], live_paths=[conflict.as_posix()]) where conflict = root/'release.stage' containing genuine current content
hidden_case.raw_output:
HIDDEN CASE: pointer-referenced file with debris-like suffix -> debris
Full record: {'path': '.../release.stage', 'classification': 'debris', 'reason': 'explicit debris marker or transient suffix', 'sha256': '88e4042654ead0e745a547aa4beeaca52c06be20e1432a6e1b66c5b2753aae8c', 'bytes': 57}
hidden_case.analysis: Suffix-based debris heuristics take priority over explicit pointer/current-path evidence in the classification precedence order. A file the pointer graph confirms is live is still misclassified as debris purely because of its filename suffix. This undermines the hypothesis's core claim of using pointer evidence to distinguish debris from live content.

additional_findings: Even after the corrective work in the final commit, the detector's own per_surface_verdicts.json states: 'The detector read all 93 blobs through git plumbing; every artifact classified unresolved, so real live/debris detection power was not demonstrated' -- i.e. the producer's own later evidence concedes the marker-based detection mechanism has no power to classify real production content (it only classifies synthetic fixtures embedding literal 'OBZIO-LIVE-SURFACE' / 'OBZIO-TRANSPORT-DEBRIS' byte markers).

producer_claim.evidence_text: python3 -I workstreams/po03/attempts/po03-wa-b2e7-034-transport-debris-detector/test_transport_debris_detector.py ran 2 tests and reported OK, including missing-root handling. A direct read-only surface check reported _transport ABSENT, packs ABSENT and modules ABSENT, so no repository debris classification was claimed.

divergence_reason: The producer claimed NOT_SUPPORTED on the premise that packs is absent from the repository. This premise is false: packs/** exists with 93 real files at the pinned commit 1e6f53c323f8326d12af213557082a3665991f19, which the producer's own later-committed code and evidence files (scan_git_tree, per_surface_verdicts.json, real_pack_output.json, all present in the same subtree at the reviewed ref) independently prove. The recorded manifest/result documents were never reconciled with this later work, so the final claimed verdict is stale and its central premise is refuted by evidence committed in the same subtree. Independent verdict is FAIL rather than NOT_SUPPORTED because concrete acceptance criteria are violated (incomplete artifact manifest; a false claim left as the operative evidence) rather than the hypothesis being merely untestable.

vacuous_test_check.method: Traced whether a stub always returning 'unresolved' for every file would pass the producer's own tests; test 1 asserts specific counts of live=1/debris=1/unresolved=1 which a fixed stub would fail.

disposition_reason: The committed result document for this unit is stale and materially misleading: it asserts a false 'packs ABSENT' premise that the unit's own later, committed evidence refutes, and the artifact manifest omits two real evidence files (per_surface_verdicts.json, real_pack_output.json) present in the same owned subtree at the reviewed ref. This directly violates the acceptance criteria 'artifact manifest lists every artifact with SHA-256 and exact byte count' and 'no value, hash, metric or provider capability is invented' (a refuted claim left standing functions the same way). Separately, the hidden case shows the detector's suffix-priority classification logic can misclassify pointer-confirmed live content as debris.
